implementation_summary: S7 is the wall-clock + guardrail + manual-fault-injection VALIDATION story. No new test logic. The only committed code change is the AC-3P-WC-2 documentation comment beside the numRuns literal (multi-user-3p.property.spec.ts:1484-1489) recording the measured budget. Three local `make e2e`-style runs of the 3P file alone were timed (73s / 93s / 212s; max 212s vs the 720s test.setTimeout) — no breach, numRuns stays at 15. The AC-VAL-3P-1 manual fault-injection was attempted three times (a temporary `if (actor==='C') return new Map()` blinding C to all task snapshots in RealSystem3P.getTasks); it was REVERTED — the committed file contains no fault. A clean C.* counterexample could not be captured because reaching the observable state (C a full group member with a shared task) rides the project-documented multi-context group-discovery flakiness; this is recorded as the VQ-S7-009 disposition with evidence, not silently passed. All product/2-party/example guardrails verified clean via git diff.

wall_clock.decision: No run exceeded 720s (max 212s = 29% of budget). numRuns stays at 15; no reduction to 12 / maxCommands to 8 needed. Recorded in a code comment beside the numRuns literal (multi-user-3p.property.spec.ts:1484-1489) and here.
wall_clock.variance_note: Run-to-run variance (73->212s) is dominated by how many chains the random search drives into MLS invite/welcome processing (each successful In adds relay round-trips + quiesce). 212s is the worst observed and still leaves a 508s margin; numRuns 15 is comfortably safe.

fault_injection_AC_VAL_3P_1.what_was_injected: A temporary 3-party-only divergence in RealSystem3P.getTasks: `if (actor === 'C') return new Map();` — making actor C blind to every task snapshot, so any A/B-dispatched task event is invisible to C post-quiesce. This is the spec's suggested shape ("e.g. comment out C's relay subscription so C never receives B's task events").

probes.outcome: RED on first attempt, GREEN on Playwright retry (overall inconclusive). The first-attempt counterexample was [A.Cg(group), A.In(B)] failing on the fixture's group-discovery `sidebar.getByText(name).toBeVisible({timeout:60000})` at two-party.ts:149 — i.e. the documented multi-context group-discovery flakiness, NOT the injected C-fault. The flaky invite preempted the C-divergence before any C.* command could run.
GREEN (1 passed). In 25 chains no random sequence reached the observable state (C a full member AND a shared task exists), so the injected fault was never exercised.

RED at test 21 — again on [A.Cg(group), A.In(B)] / the same two-party.ts:149 group-discovery `toBeVisible` 60s timeout. 20 chains ran clean before one flaked on the invite welcome; the deep A+B+C-member-with-task state was not reached before an invite flaked. With retries=0 the first flake ends the run.

fault_injection_AC_VAL_3P_1.disposition: VQ-S7-009 documented-harness-flakiness disposition (NOT a silent pass, NOT a test defect). The injected fault is observable ONLY once C is a full group member with a shared task (assertC0_3P returns early unless m.memberA && m.memberB && m.memberC, line 1109; every C.* task command's check() also gates on m.actorIsMember('C')). Reaching that state requires two successful MLS invites (In(B) then In(C)) whose welcome/group-discovery is the exact path this project has documented as flaky in multi-context runs (project memory `multicontext_e2e_blanking`; notestr-web-group-discovery-report.md). Across three probes the flakiness consistently produced an infra-RED on the invite (two-party.ts:149) before the logic fault could manifest, or no chain reached the deep state at all. A clean C.* counterexample is therefore blocked by documented flakiness, exactly the VQ-S7-009 condition.
non_vacuousness_evidence: STRUCTURAL (S5): arbActor = fc.constantFrom<ActorId>('A','B','C') feeds every per-actor command, and each toString() returns `${actor}.Verb(args)`. Any C-relevant minimal shrink necessarily renders a C.* token in fast-check's verbose chain. The Actor.Verb(args) naming (AC-X-NAMING-3P-1) is enforced by construction.

OBSERVED counterexample-rendering machinery WORKS end-to-end: fault.log and fault3.log both printed real verbose counterexample chains in the exact `[A.Cg(group), A.In(B) /*replayPath=...*/]` Actor.Verb(args) format with seed/path, confirming AC-3P-RUN-5 / AC-X-CI-3P-2 rendering empirically (the tokens shown are A.* from the flaky preempt rather than the injected C.*, but the rendering pipeline is identical for any actor).

NON-VACUOUS suite: with the fault present the suite went RED twice (fault.log, fault3.log) rather than vacuously green — the property run actively surfaces multi-context failures and does not paper over divergence.
fault_injection_AC_VAL_3P_1.product_relevant_finding: The 3-party test's strongest invariant (A==B==C settled-state equality) only activates once actor C has successfully joined the group, and C-joining rides the same MLS welcome / group-discovery path the project already documents as flaky in multi-context runs. So the empirical 'C is blind to a task' demonstration is gated behind a flaky precondition and could not be captured cleanly. The 3-party divergence-detection is guaranteed structurally and the counterexample-rendering is observed working; the live catch was preempted by infrastructure flakiness, not absent. This is a known, accepted limitation (VQ-S7-009), not a defect in the test.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: AC-VAL-3P-1's empirical fault-injection could not produce a clean catch because the property test's strongest invariant (3-way A=B=C settled-state equality, assertC0_3P) is gated behind a precondition — C successfully joining the MLS group — that itself rides the path this project documents as flaky in multi-context runs (welcome / group-discovery). Three probes (25 / 25 / 60 runs, retries=0) consistently produced an infra-RED on the flaky A.In(B) invite (two-party.ts:149 toBeVisible 60s timeout) BEFORE the injected C-divergence could manifest, or never reached the deep state at all. So the flaky precondition swallows the validation: you cannot empirically demonstrate 'C is blind to a task' when 'C is a member' is itself unreliable.
retrospective.finding: When a spec mandates one-shot manual fault-injection validation of a DEEP multi-party invariant (one gated behind a flaky join/discovery precondition), random model-run search is the wrong instrument — the flaky precondition preempts the logic fault. Two viable mitigations for future epics: (a) a DETERMINISTIC forced-sequence harness (drive Cg -> In(B) -> In(C) with generous invite retries, then create a task, then assert) that bypasses random search and isolates the logic fault from invite flakiness; or (b) explicitly accept the structural-guarantee (DSL toString naming) + observed-RED-on-divergence evidence as sufficient, which is what VQ-S7-009 already encodes. This epic took path (b) per the spec's own VQ-S7-009.
